text:
Bitcoin is showing resilience near $63,800 despite a 1.2% contraction in total digital asset market capitalization to $2.14 trillion. This broader "risk-off" retreat was largely catalyzed by new U.S. military strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, which injected immediate volatility into global energy and equity markets. While the Crypto Fear & Greed Index remains suppressed at 25, institutional foundation-building continues unabated, highlighted by Circle receiving rare U.S. regulatory approval to establish a national trust bank.

The macroeconomic environment remains the dominant force dictating capital flows. With the Federal Reserve maintaining its target funds rate at 3.50%–3.75% amidst stubbornly sticky core inflation, market participants are heavily weighing the upcoming July 28 FOMC meeting. The potential for prolonged elevated interest rates continues to structurally constrain non-yielding digital assets, closely tethering Bitcoin's near-term trajectory to the performance of traditional equities and the strength of the U.S. dollar.
